title: French Civil Code Article 1112: negotiations
summary: The assigned translation combines freedom to initiate, conduct, and end negotiations with a mandatory requirement of good faith.
notes:
The translation permits damages where negotiations are at fault but excludes compensation for the benefits expected from the unmade contract and for the lost chance of obtaining those benefits. This makes it useful to separate a freedom to decline a final transaction from responsibility for the way negotiations are conducted.

Compare the provision with Dixon, Cyberchron, and Channel Home. Identify whether liability rests on reliance, an agreed negotiating commitment, or the regulation of negotiating conduct. Then identify the permissible measure of recovery. The translation is presented as comparative material, not as the rule governing a domestic U.S. dispute.

textbookImport.basis: Paraphrase of the actual Fall 2026 course supplement. The source retains its own date and legal context; no current-law verification.

topics.precontractual-liability: The article directly regulates negotiating conduct without guaranteeing a completed agreement.
topics.good-faith: It makes good faith a requirement in negotiations.
